Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Aegis Insurance Group Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Aegis Insurance Group's Second Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Lee, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Taylor, Chief Investment Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to David Johnson.

David Johnson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Aegis Insurance Group's performance for the second quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by realized and unrealized gains on our investments, disciplined share repurchase activity, attractive investment income yields, positive impacts from pricing changes on premium volume, a rock-solid capital position with elevated statutory surplus levels, and impressive policy retention rates across our major product lines. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our new AI-powered cyber insurance platform and its rapid adoption in commercial lines, which is already contributing to margin expansion.

Sarah, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.45 per diluted share. Key drivers of our financial performance included robust investment returns, strategic capital returns to shareholders, premium growth fueled by rate discipline, strong customer loyalty metrics, and a fortress-like balance sheet.

Let me start by diving deeper into our investment performance, particularly our realized and unrealized gains and losses on investments, which added a net positive $420 million to our bottom line this quarter. Our $162 billion investment portfolio continues to power our float generation and enable competitive pricing across our property & casualty and life & annuity lines. We manage it through a rigorous asset-liability management framework, aiming for a book yield around 4.2% while keeping duration conservative at 5.8 years to align with our long-tail liabilities.

On the headline numbers, we posted $285 million in realized gains, a 15% increase from the $248 million in the first quarter, mainly from strategic sales in our fixed income holdings. This was partially offset by $135 million in unrealized losses, which improved 22% from Q1's $173 million mark-to-market pressures as bond markets steadied following the Fed's pause on rate hikes. That nets to the $420 million gain, equivalent to 102 basis points of annualized portfolio return—outperforming the peer average of 85 basis points according to SNL Financial.

Breaking down the realized gains by asset class, fixed income led with $210 million, representing 74% of the total. We captured these by repositioning $2.1 billion from intermediate investment-grade corporates—such as Apple bonds and JPMorgan financials—where yields had tightened from 5.2% at purchase to 4.8%; our yield-to-worst now sits at 5.1% after the rebalance. Equities added $55 million by scaling back S&P 500 index positions during the tech rally, selling 1.2 million shares of NVIDIA and Microsoft to lock in 12% year-to-date gains. Our alternatives allocation, including $8.5 billion in private credit and infrastructure through vehicles like Blackstone's BCRED and Brookfield's infrastructure funds, contributed $20 million from exits in renewable energy projects.

For unrealized movements, the $135 million loss stemmed from duration extension in Treasuries and agency MBS as the 10-year yield rose 12 basis points to 4.35%. Our core fixed income, 68% of the portfolio, delivered a -0.8% total return, with losses focused in longer-duration assets averaging 7.2 years. Equities were essentially flat, with a minor $15 million dip in our 12% allocation, offset by the Magnificent Seven's 18% quarterly surge. Positively, our $12 billion alternatives sleeve generated a 1.2% unrealized gain from NAV increases in direct lending, where spreads widened to 550 basis points over SOFR as banks pulled back.

Year-over-year, this net gain marks a 133% improvement from Q2 2023's $180 million, lapping last year's equity weakness from the regional banking stresses. Trailing twelve-month total investment return now stands at 5.6%, combining $912 million in net investment income with these gains and losses. Volatility has eased, with portfolio VaR at 99% confidence down to 4.2% from 5.1% a year ago, thanks to our hedging including $3.2 billion in interest rate swaps and Treasury futures that limit duration shifts to plus or minus 0.5 years.

Regionally, U.S. assets at 72% of the portfolio drove 80% of gains, highlighted by strong munis—AAA/AA quality yielding 4.0% tax-equivalent—and RMBS from life annuity runoff. Europe, 15% of the book, dealt with ECB tightening headwinds, posting €85 million equivalent unrealized losses on German Bunds, but our UK gilts overweight yielded £120 million in realized gains after the BOE's pivot. Asia-Pacific, with 10% exposure, held resilient at +0.9% unrealized from JGBs and Aussie semis amid yen carry unwind, plus a 2.1% markup on $1.8 billion Indian infrastructure debt through ICICI Prudential funds. We keep emerging markets underweight at 3%, sticking to BBB-rated credits to sidestep FX risks.

On initiatives, our ALM tech stack, powered by BlackRock's Aladdin for scenario modeling, has optimized convexity. This quarter, we expanded our equity overlay with $500 million in total return swaps on the Russell 2000 for a 200 basis point pickup over cash. ESG progress shows 28% of assets meeting SFDR Article 8/9 standards, including $4.2 billion in green bonds from issuers like Ørsted and Enel at a 20 basis point yield premium. Credit quality is top-tier: 92% investment grade, A- average rating, with NAIC 3+ non-performers at 0.8%.

Strategically, we're geared for a soft landing. With policy duration at 6.1 years versus liabilities at 6.4, we're easing into 5-10 year corporates for a year-end book yield of 4.6%. Expect $300-400 million more realized gains in the second half from equity trims if the S&P reaches 5,800, while derivatives shield against 10-year yields above 4.5%. This bolsters our 12-14% ROE target, funding growth in cyber insurance and longevity swaps. Relative to Progressive or Allianz, our 1.15x reserve coverage and active management shine in a 3.8% risk-free rate backdrop.

Transitioning to our investment income yield, another key pillar, we achieved 4.35% for the quarter—up 25 basis points sequentially and 65 basis points year-over-year from 3.70% in Q2 2023. This is our best quarterly figure since pre-pandemic, fueled by reinvesting maturities at higher rates during the Fed's hikes and a steepening curve. Trailing twelve months, it's 4.12%, cushioning P&C combined ratio pressures.

Our $185 billion general account portfolio is conservatively allocated: 78% fixed maturities, 12% equities, 7% alternatives, and the rest in shorts and cash. Fixed income blended at 4.62%, with investment-grade corporates—45% of that sleeve—at 4.85% (up from 4.45%), overweighting A and BBB in utilities and financials like Southern Company or JPMorgan analogs for 140 basis point spreads over Treasuries. Treasuries and agency MBS at 25% yielded 4.10% with 5.2-year duration matching liabilities. Munis and structured credit at 20% hit 5.15%, powered by AA CLOs and insured munis; CLOs at 4% of portfolio offer 6.2% floating. Alternatives like Ares and Blackstone private credit yielded 6.8%, mid-teens gross.

Equities from dividend aristocrats like Procter & Gamble and S&P ETF stakes added 2.1%, post some derisking after April's rally. U.S. assets (72%) captured the 10-year at 4.4%; Europe (18%) at 3.8% shifted to UK gilts and covered bonds for 30 basis point lift; Asia-Pacific (8%) at 2.9% stabilized with JGBs and AUD floaters, 85% FX hedged limiting drag to 5 basis points.

Technically, forward-starting swaps locked 4.7% on $12 billion maturities; ESG covers 15% ($28 billion) in green bonds with Solvency II/NAIC benefits; laddering trimmed duration to 5.4 years at 1.25x reserve coverage. Unlike MetLife's legacy drag, 65% of our book yields over 4%. Full-year guide: 4.4-4.6%, with $25 billion liquidity buffer.

Now, on capital deployment, our share repurchase activity totaled $325 million this quarter, or 7.2 million shares at $45.14 average—year-to-date matching that, using 16% of our $2 billion Board-authorized program from November 2023. We use a 10b5-1 plan with algo collars targeting 5-10% below 12-month VWAP, accretive to BVPS at 18% embedded value discount ($68/share).

North America took 85% ($276 million), from P&C and group life free cash flow of $1.2 billion on 92.8% ex-cat combined ratio. At 512% RBC versus 400% target, higher rates boosted investment income 14% YoY to $450 million. Europe $38 million (12%) from UK motor/health post 30% lower cats and IFRS 17; Asia-Pacific $11 million from Hong Kong JV VONB up 22%.

Buybacks accretes $0.12 EPS/$1.45 TBVPS per $100 million, retiring 4.2% shares for 14% ROTCE target. Balanced with 8% dividend hike to $0.42 and $4.8 billion M&A powder. Q1 accelerated 25% QoQ on inflation pessimism; ex-cat loss ratio 62.5% with 15% hikes. Remaining $1.675 billion authorizes $800 million-$1 billion full-year on $3.8 billion FCFF.

Regarding premium volume, pricing changes drove 8.2% YoY GWP growth to $12.5 billion, beating 5-6% industry. Personal lines (55%, $6.9 billion up 9.5%) saw 6.8% rates: auto 7.2% on 12% repairs, retention 88%; homeowners 8.1% up 12.3%. Commercial (35%, $4.4 billion up 7.1%) 4.9% rates, workers' comp 5.6%, GL 6.2%, retention 91%. U.S. 11% growth, Europe 4% with 28% UBI, Asia 15%. GLMs, cat models, -0.4x auto elasticity guide 7-9% Q3.

Policy retention rates hit 89.2% overall, up 110 bps QoQ/240 bps YoY, beating 87.5% industry. Personal auto 92.4% (Snapshot telematics 28%), homeowners 88.7%, commercial P&C 85.6% (88.2% middle-market), specialty 87.1% (cyber 89%), life/annuity 91.3%. U.S. Northeast/Midwest 90.1%, Southeast 86.8%. Digital app 65% renewals, GLMs, Rewards+ drive 89-90% Q3.

Finally, our capital position shows $18.7 billion statutory surplus at year-end 2023, up 11% YoY/9% five-year CAGR. RBC 512% consolidated (P&C 545%, life 428%). Earnings $2.1 billion, 92.6% combined, $1.8 billion investments. U.S. bedrock, Europe 185% SCR, Asia 15% growth. Reinsurance, cat bonds, ERM platform support 8-10% 2024 growth.

Our combined ratio was 92.5%. Investment income was $450 million, strong in fixed income. Capital at 520% RBC.

Michael, over to you for underwriting.

Michael Lee: Thank you, Sarah. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophes and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced telematics and AI-driven pricing models.

Robert Taylor: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for participants: Please press star then one on your touchtone phone to queue a question. Our first question comes from Alex Green with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Green: Good morning. Can you provide more color on your investment performance, especially the alternatives allocation?

David Johnson: Good morning, Alex. Happy to elaborate. As Sarah detailed, our alternatives have been a standout, with private credit spreads widening and infrastructure NAV uplifts providing diversification. We're selective, focusing on high-quality managers like Blackstone and Brookfield, and it complements our fixed income core without excessive risk. This positions us well for ongoing volatility.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jamie Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jamie Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of higher interest rates on your business?

Sarah Chen: Good morning, Jamie. Higher rates have been a tailwind across the board. They've boosted our investment yield to 4.35%, enhanced reinvestment opportunities, and strengthened our surplus growth to support buybacks and dividends. On liabilities, our duration matching minimizes negative convexity, and for policyholders, it supports competitive crediting in annuities. Overall, it reinforces our float advantage.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks: Good morning. What is the expected impact of new regulatory changes in catastrophe modeling on your underwriting strategy?

Michael Lee: Good morning, Taylor. The updates to cat modeling standards, like RMS v17 enhancements, are prompting more granular risk assessment, but we're ahead of the curve. We've already integrated climate scenarios into our GLMs and reinsurance towers, maintaining our 92.5% combined while growing exposure selectively in non-peak zones. No major strategy shift; it actually sharpens our edge over less tech-forward peers.

Operator: Our next question is a follow-up from Alex Green with Goldman Sachs.

Alex Green: Thanks. On retention, how sustainable is 89%+ with ongoing rate hikes?

Sarah Chen: Great question, Alex. Sustainability comes from our multi-pillar approach: digital renewals at 65%, loyalty programs like Rewards+ delivering 2.5x uplift, and precise pricing via ML that holds loss ratios steady. Bundling and telematics keep elasticity low, and we're targeting 92% in auto by year-end with EV UBI. Industry-leading at 240 bps YoY outperformance.

Operator: Seeing no further questions at this time...

David Johnson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Aegis Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
